body.translated_text: <s>Caryāmelāvaṇapradīpa</s> (The Lamp for the Integration of Practices)
1. First Chapter
Oṃ! Homage to the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>!

children.translated_text: Homage to that which is pure in its nature, equal to space; homage to what is complete, without syllable, and inexpressible.
Homage to the <s>Sugata</s> who has not yet come and who pervades all; homage to that which is entirely and completely empty.

body.translated_text: "One should rely on the meaning, not on the words as they are."

body.text:
tantre-
caturaśītisāhasre dharmaskandhe mahāmuneḥ /
tattvaṃ vai ye na jānanti sarve te niṣphalāya vai // iti /
body.translated_text:
In the <s>Tantra</s>:
"Among the eighty-four thousand <s>dharma</s>-aggregates of the Great Sage,
those who do not know the truth — all of them are indeed fruitless."

body.text:
ata āha-
ādikarmikasandhānaṃ paramārthāvatāraṇe /
upāyaścaiva saṃbuddhaiḥ sopānamiva nirmitaḥ // iti /
body.translated_text:
Therefore it is said:
"For beginners, the entry into ultimate reality —
the <s>Sambuddhas</s> have constructed skillful means like a staircase."
End of the first chapter: The Awakening, Integration, and Resolution of Doubts. // 1 //
2. Second Chapter

children.translated_text: The five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), in brief, are proclaimed as the five <s>Buddhas</s>.
The <s>vajra</s> sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) themselves are the supreme <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>maṇḍala</s>.
Earth is known as <s>Locanā</s>; the water element is remembered as <s>Māmakī</s>.
Fire is called <s>Pāṇḍarā</s>; wind is proclaimed as <s>Tārā</s>.

body.translated_text: Through form, sound, and the other sense-objects, the <s>mantrin</s> should always meditate on the deity.
Thus it is spoken by the Blessed One in the <s>Śrī Guhyasamāja Mahāyogatantra</s>.

children.text: kulāḥ śatavidhāḥ proktāḥ saṃkṣepeṇa tu pañcadhā /
children.translated_text: The families (<s>kula</s>) are said to be a hundredfold, but in brief they are fivefold.
They again become threefold through the division of body, speech, and mind.

body.translated_text: "The five aggregates, in brief, are proclaimed as the five <s>Buddhas</s>."

Depending on the five hearts, emanating from the five bodies,
conjoined with the five winds, producing the enjoyment of the five desires.

children.translated_text: Through movement, through <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), through the sense-doors and channels,
that which always moves in time is called <s>prāṇa</s> (the vital breath).
Of wind, urine, feces, semen, and the like,
that which carries them away is called <s>apāna</s> (the downward breath), always observed by yogins.

children.text: aśitaṃ khāditaṃ lehyaṃ peyaṃ coṣyañca sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: What is eaten, chewed, licked, drunk, and sucked from all sides —

children.text: samānayati yo nityaṃ samāna iti cocyate //
children.translated_text: that which always equalizes them is called <s>samāna</s> (the equalizing breath).
Through upward movement, through gathering, through the consumption of food and drink —
one who knows the function of <s>udāna</s> (the upward breath) is conjoined with knowledge.
Pervading, sustaining, and also going and coming —
because it pervades all the joints, it is called <s>vyāna</s> (the diffusive breath).
Earth is known as <s>Locanā</s>; the water element is remembered as <s>Māmakī</s>.
Fire is called <s>Pāṇḍarā</s>; wind is proclaimed as <s>Tārā</s>.

children.text: skandhaśca dhātuśca tathaivendriyaṃ ca pañcaiva pañcaiva kṛtaprabhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: The aggregates, elements, and likewise the faculties — each is fivefold, made into fivefold divisions.
Each empowered by a <s>Tathāgata</s> — whence do the actions of <s>saṃsāra</s> arise?

children.text: tathā sabāhyā viṣayāśca pañca ekaikaśaḥ pañcatathāgataiśca /
children.translated_text: Likewise the five external sense-objects, each by the five <s>Tathāgatas</s>,
are always empowered, each in their own domain, and the three knowledges also rest upon the five.

body.text:
khadhātumadhyagataṃ cintenmaṇḍalaṃ sarvavajrajam /
saṃhāraṃ ca prakurvīta yadīcchecchāntavajradhṛg // iti /
pañcātmakaṃ pañcabhireva bhūtairdṛṣṭaṃ narāṇāṃ niyataṃ śarīram /
tabhdāvabhāvairniyataṃ svacittaṃ prabhāvayantaḥ prabhavanti buddhāḥ // iti /

khasamatantre 'pyāha-
pañcabuddhātmaku sarvajago 'yaṃ paśyasu citraku nāṭaku divyam /
yatra hi eku mahāsuhanāmā nṛtyati eku aneka rasena // iti /
body.translated_text:
In the <s>Khasamatantra</s> also it is said:
"This entire world is of the nature of the five <s>Buddhas</s> — behold this marvelous divine spectacle!
Wherein the One called Great Bliss dances alone with manifold flavors."
"In brief, they are fivefold."

children.translated_text: Through the resolution of body, speech, and mind, intrinsic nature is not apprehended.
Through the practice of <s>mantra</s>-form, there is neither awakening nor meditation.

body.text:
vicāryedaṃ samāsena kāyavākcittalakṣaṇam /
bhāvayedvidhisaṃyogaṃ samādhiṃ mantrakalpitam // iti /

children.translated_text: Yoga does not arise in reflections, consecrated images, and the like.
Through the great yoga of <s>bodhicitta</s>, the yogins become deities.

body.translated_text:
One should examine in brief the characteristics of body, speech, and mind;
one should cultivate the <s>samādhi</s> conceived by <s>mantra</s> in conjunction with the proper method.

body.text:
ātmā vai sarvabuddhatvaṃ sattvasauritvameva ca /
svādhidaivadya(ta)yogena tasmādātmaiva sādhayet // iti /

children.translated_text: Through the body resolved upon <s>mantra</s>, through speech, and impelled in mind,
one should accomplish the supreme <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), dear and delighting to the mind.

body.translated_text:
The self is indeed all Buddhahood and also the essence of beings;
through the yoga of one's own tutelary deity, therefore, one should accomplish the self.
End of the second chapter: The Integration and Resolution of Doubts concerning the Seclusion of Body. // 2 //
3. Third Chapter

body.text:
pañcavarṇaṃ mahāratnaṃ sarṣapasthūlamātrakam /
nāsikāgre prayatnena bhāvayedyogataḥ sadā // iti /
pañcajñānamayaṃ śvāsaṃ pañcabhūtasvabhāvakam //
body.translated_text:
One should always meditate through yoga, with effort, on a great jewel of five colors,
the size of a mustard seed, at the tip of the nose.
The breath, consisting of the five knowledges, of the nature of the five elements —

children.translated_text: having exhaled it, one should visualize it in drop-form at the tip of the lotus-nose.
The great jewel of five colors is known as <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control).
Then the Blessed One, the great <s>Vajrin</s>, who speaks the meaning of <s>vajra</s> recitation,
duly replied, having bowed to the One, the Guru of the world.

body.translated_text: "This <s>bodhicitta</s> has been revealed merely as worldly tradition.
How then will future practitioners attain the supramundane?

children.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s> was taught by you for the abandonment of all views.

children.text: tat kathaṃ bodhicittaṃ tu sā dṛṣṭiḥ sudṛḍhīkṛtā //
children.translated_text: How then is <s>bodhicitta</s> that very view, firmly established?"
Those deluded by intentional language do not understand the intended meaning;

children.text: yathārutaṃ te gṛṇhanti tathaiva hi pacanti ca //
children.translated_text: they grasp it literally and cook it just as it is.

children.text: atha bhagavān viśvo vajrapāṇiṃ vadet tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Viśva</s> (Universal) said to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>:

children.text: sādhu sādhu ca guhyeśa vyākṛtāgāmikā tvayā //
children.translated_text: "Well done, well done, O Lord of Secrets! You have prophesied for future practitioners.
<s>Bodhicitta</s> is wind, established in space,
the vital principle of beings — of five natures and ten designations.
Called the twelve limbs of dependent origination, it becomes threefold by nature.
Predominant among all faculties, this <s>bodhicitta</s> is designated as wind.
It is always called 'unmanifest' and 'subtle,' as well as 'manifest.'
Based on it, beings perform actions and engage with sense-objects and the like.
Pacifying, enriching, subjugating, and destroying —
all that proceeds from <s>bodhicitta</s>, based on the abode of the three realities.
However many varied conventions of the world there may be,
conceptualizations always arise from <s>bodhicitta</s>, from wind.
The dharma of happiness, suffering, and so forth is produced from the seed alone.
<s>Bodhicitta</s> is of that nature — like the non-dual arising of the aggregates and so forth.

body.translated_text: Through the single yoga of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and means (<s>upāya</s>), <s>bodhicitta</s> becomes the world.
The Lord himself utters it spontaneously, without meditation or study.

children.translated_text: Through the division of day and night, through the application of moon and sun,
the breath pervades the world — <s>bodhicitta</s> is the one wind.
Those called <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s>,
and <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Kṛkara</s>, <s>Devadatta</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s> —

body.translated_text: Having abandoned the fruit of merit and demerit, one becomes like space.

body.text: kṛtvaitadātmano bimbaṃ strītattvaṃ nirmāya te punaḥ // iti /

children.translated_text: <s>Koṭākṣa</s>, <s>Koṭava</s>, <s>Koṭa</s>, <s>Koṭābha</s>, and <s>Koṭīraka</s>,
<s>Kolākṣa</s>, <s>Kolāva</s>, <s>Kola</s>, <s>Kolābha</s>, and <s>Kali</s> —

body.translated_text: having made this image of the self, and again having fashioned the feminine principle —

children.translated_text: born from the opening of the nostrils, established in the five <s>Buddha</s>-families,
the five winds, moving upward, always course through the body.
Through the conventional movement of the nose, having emerged from its door,
they are fourfold: left, right, both together, and still.
From the right, the element flows forth — it is the <s>maṇḍala</s> of fire,
of red color — this aspect moves under the lordship of <s>Padmanātha</s> (Lord of the Lotus).
From the left, the element flows forth, issuing from the wind <s>maṇḍala</s>,
green, of dark appearance — it moves under the lordship of <s>Karmanātha</s> (Lord of Action).
The element flowing from both together is golden in color, with the trident,
and it is the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Mahendra</s> — it moves under the lordship of <s>Ratnanātha</s> (Lord of the Jewel).
The still element does not flow — in an instant it is the water <s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling pure crystal — it moves under the lordship of <s>Vajranātha</s> (Lord of the Vajra).
Having gathered all the elements, supported as the base and the supported,
the great body of <s>Vairocana</s> moves forth at the time of death.
One should always recite this four-<s>maṇḍala</s> practice with concentration,
day and night — for <s>mantrins</s>, the recitation is counted as constant recitation.
Beginning from one, in the middle of nine, he who is not bound by ten —

children.text: tamabaddhaṃ vijānīyāt sa vetti paramaṃ padam //
children.translated_text: know that unbound one; he knows the supreme state.
The vowels, consonants, and letter-parts, following the count of nine,
unbound in their mutual conjunction — he who knows this is the Guru of the world.
He who desires <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) through the <s>Buddha</s>-path, the wealth of the fruit of liberation,
he attains that very thing — formless, devoid of form.
Conjoined with the ultimate point, established in the sixteenth <s>kalā</s>,
conjoined with the five-times-five, yoked with the four courses.
With <s>anusvāra</s>, with lengthening, having the conjunction and elision of qualities,

children.text: hrasvaṃ samastavākyaṃ syānna cānekaṃ na caikakam //
children.translated_text: short, it would be a complete sentence — neither many nor one.
Whatever is to be done by one desiring <s>siddhi</s> through the meaning of the letter 'ya,'
through the triad beginning with 'ra' alone, the activity of the world proceeds.

children.text: ye varṇāḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ proktā abhimukhāśca ye punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those letters that are spoken as posterior, and those again that are anterior,
they are feminine, masculine, and neuter — conceived through the elements and other categories.
Joined below and above, known through wisdom, they are set in order.
It is taught through the six: the four, three, three, and one arise from the single essence without own-nature.
Joining the three and so forth for the primary purpose, knowledge of the three times arises.
Knowing it as twofold—like dreams and <s>Indra</s>'s net—one should act in the three realms of the world.
This <s>mantra</s> is the <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal), arising from the own-nature of non-own-nature.
Then the transformed form is that which is perceived as the deity.
Conventional, abiding in the three realities, characterized by natural syllables,
inexpressible and unutterable—this is the supreme <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening).
That itself, being one in the three, is without going out and without coming in,
without cessation, peaceful, and free from eternalism and nihilism.
Free from conceptualization, made by the knower of the three times, characterized by the indivisibility of space,
this is indeed the ultimate, characterized by being known through direct personal experience.
In all activities whatsoever—sitting and so forth—the knower of <s>yoga</s>
should always recite that which is inexpressible, unutterable, and beyond the three times.
The recitations beginning with <s>Pāṇḍarā</s> are taught as two hundred and twenty-five,
properly multiplied by four: four <s>yogas</s>, nine hundred.
The nine hundred that is seen, through twenty-four cycles,
from the arising thereof, becomes twenty thousand and sixteen hundred.
Thus, in the secret <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight language), the subtle <s>yoga</s> has been revealed.
Though it transcends meditation and study, even so it is called recitation.

body.text:
akāraḥ sarvavarṇāgryo mahārthaḥ paramākṣaraḥ /
mahāprāṇo hyanutpādo vāgudāhāravarjitaḥ /
sarvābhilāpahetvagryaḥ sarvavāksuprabhāsvaraḥ // iti /
jvalantaṃ dīpasadṛśaṃ hṛdi madhyamanāhatam /
akṣaraṃ paramaṃ sūkṣmam akāraṃ paramaṃ prabhum // iti /
dharmā ime śabdarutena vyākṛtā
dharmaśca śabdaśca hi nātra labhyate /
na caikatāṃ cāpyavatīrya dharmatām
anuttarāṃ kṣāntivarāṃ spṛśiṣyate // iti /
body.translated_text:
The letter 'a' is the foremost of all letters, of great meaning, the supreme syllable,
the great <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is indeed non-arising, free from verbal expression,
the foremost cause of all designation, the most luminous of all speech. Thus:
Blazing like a lamp, in the heart, the central unstruck
syllable, supreme and subtle, the letter 'a', the supreme lord. Thus:
These <s>dharmas</s> are explained by the sound of words,
yet neither <s>dharma</s> nor word can be found here.
Not descending into the oneness of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality),
one will touch the supreme, best patience. Thus:
End of the third chapter: the section on resolving doubts regarding the integration of speech-isolation.
4. Fourth Chapter

body.text:
dūraṅgamekacaramaśarīraṃ guhāśayam /
ye cittaṃ sanniveśayanti mucyante mārabandhanād // iti /
pratītyotpadyate yadyadindriyairviṣayairmanaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Far-ranging, solitary, bodiless, dwelling in the cave—
those who direct the mind are freed from the bonds of <s>Māra</s>. Thus:
That which arises dependently through the sense faculties and objects is the mind.
That mind is known as eighty, with the syllable 'sra' serving the purpose of protection. Thus:

children.translated_text: <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), being mere awareness, has the characteristic of being like space,
yet there are divisions of it, in the form of twilight, night, and day.
Luminosity and non-luminosity, and also the perception of luminosity—
the mind is said to be threefold; its support is now explained.

body.translated_text: Through <s>vāyu</s> (wind) in subtle form, knowledge has become intermingled.
Going forth through the pathways of the sense faculties, it apprehends objects.

children.translated_text: When the <s>vāyu</s> is joined with appearance, it becomes a vehicle,
then all its natures become completely disordered.

body.text: yatra yatra sthito vāyustāṃ tāṃ prakṛtimudvaheta // iti /
body.translated_text: Wherever the <s>vāyu</s> abides, it carries forth that particular nature. Thus:
End of the fourth chapter: the section on resolving doubts regarding the integration of mind-isolation.
5. Fifth Chapter

children.translated_text: Just as the many clouds, of various shapes and colors,
having arisen from the expanse of the sky, dissolve back into it,
so too all natures, caused by the three appearances,
having pervaded all objects, enter into the luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>).
Thus, by nature, from consciousness, covered by the veil of ignorance,
having performed wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>, they wander in the five destinies.
Having committed the <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) deeds and such, one ripens in the hells;
having performed wholesome deeds such as generosity, one is exalted in the heavens and so forth.
Having obtained thousands of infinite births again and again,
one grieves through delusion, thinking 'this is the ripening of former <s>karma</s>.'

body.text:
prakṛtyābhā[savidhinā kleśavantaśca ye janāḥ /
etajjñātvā vimu]cyanti jñānino bhavapañjarāt // iti /

children.translated_text: If all this is empty, of unborn own-nature,
how does <s>karma</s> operate here in <s>saṃsāra</s>, bringing happiness and suffering?

body.translated_text:
Those beings who have afflictions through the process of natural appearances—
knowing this, the wise are liberated from the cage of existence. Thus:

children.translated_text: Through the sense of 'I' and 'mine,' and through impurities such as <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the rest,
the foolish, projecting onto the dependent, suffer from suffering.

body.text:
cittamātramidaṃ sarvaṃ māyākārasamutthitam /
tataḥ śubhāśubhaṃ karma tato janma śubhāśubham // iti /
body.translated_text:
All this is mind-only, arisen like a magician's creation;
from that arise wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>; from that, wholesome and unwholesome births. Thus:
End of the fifth chapter: the section on resolving doubts regarding the integration of the differentiation of <s>karma</s>.
6. Sixth Chapter
Through the cultivation of reality, one obtains a body resembling a rainbow. Thus:

children.text: skandhe ca dhātvāyatanendriyādau jñānadvaye tatra samaṃ sthite 'smin /
children.translated_text: In the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), faculties, and the rest, when the two knowledges are equally established therein,

children.text: śūnye mahattve sati yaḥ prasuptaḥ svapnaṃ prapaśyet khalu vātavegāt //
children.translated_text: in the great emptiness, one who is asleep sees a dream indeed through the force of <s>vāyu</s> (wind).

children.text: svapne prabuddhe ca na cānyabhedaḥ saṃkalpayet svapnaphalābhilāṣī /
children.translated_text: Between dream and waking there is no other distinction; one who desires the fruit of dreams should not conceptualize.

children.text: rātriṃdivā svapnamupaiti jantuṃ mahīghanatve sucireṇa suptaḥ //
children.translated_text: Night and day, the being enters into dream; fallen into the density of earth, having slept for a long time.

children.text: phale na pakve kṛtakarmaṇaśca vāyuḥ punaḥ krāmati janmanīha /
children.translated_text: When the fruit is not yet ripe, and <s>karma</s> has been performed, the <s>vāyu</s> again enters into birth here.

children.text: pakvaṃ phalaṃ syād gata eva vāyuḥ paratra śīghraṃ maraṇaṃ hi loke //
children.translated_text: When the fruit is ripe, the <s>vāyu</s> has indeed departed; death comes swiftly in the world to the other realm.

children.text: yatha jinendro daśadigvyavasthito majjāsthimāṃsaṃ na ca tasya kāye /
children.translated_text: Just as the Lord of Conquerors is established in the ten directions, yet in his body there is no marrow, bone, or flesh,
he enters into the <s>dhātu</s> (element) for the benefit of beings and performs his work through an emanation-like form.

body.text:
evaṃ kramājjāgrati suptacittaḥ phalaṃ ca vāñchet savikalpajālam /
svapnopamāste khalu sarvadharmā mṛṣāmṛṣāścāpyubhayorabhāvaḥ // iti /
body.translated_text:
Thus, gradually the sleeping mind awakens, and one may desire the fruit with the net of conceptualization;
but all <s>dharmas</s> are indeed like dreams—neither true nor false, and both are absent. Thus:
End of the sixth chapter: the section on resolving doubts regarding the integration of conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>).
7. Seventh Chapter

children.translated_text: Just as a lamp placed inside a pot does not illuminate the outside,
but when that pot is broken, then the flame of the lamp shines forth,

children.text: svakāya eva hi ghaṭo dīpa eva hi tattvakam /
children.translated_text: the body itself is the pot, and reality itself is the lamp;
when broken open by the <s>guru</s>'s words, <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge becomes manifest.

body.text:
gaganaṃ gaganobhdūtamākāśākāśaṃ sa paśyati /
tathaiva hi gurorvaktrātprayogo 'yaṃ pradarśitaḥ // iti /
dharmā ime śabdarutena vyākṛtā dharmaśca śabdaśca hi nātra labhyate /
na caikatāṃ cāpyavatīrya dharmatāmanuttarāṃ kṣāntivarāṃ spṛśiṣyate // iti /

children.translated_text: Homage to you, O supreme bestower of boons, O foremost of <s>vajras</s>! Homage to you, O limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>)!
Homage to you, O womb of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāgarbha</s>)! Homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s>-awakening!

body.translated_text:
Space from space arisen—one sees space as space.
Even so, through the <s>guru</s>'s words, this practice is revealed. Thus:
These <s>dharmas</s> are explained by the sound of words,
yet neither <s>dharma</s> nor word can be found here.
Not descending into the oneness of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality),
one will touch the supreme, best patience. Thus:

children.translated_text: Grant me, O great teacher, the vision of perfect awakening,
the great knowledge of all <s>Buddhas</s>, supreme, the emptiness of all.
Grant me, O great being, that which is characterized solely by one's own experience,
freed from <s>karma</s> and birth—may I attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) right here!
Apart from your lotus feet, there is no other refuge, O Lord;
therefore be gracious, O foremost of <s>Buddhas</s>, O hero of the world, O great sage!

children.text: evaṃ stutvā tu taṃ divyamadhyeṣaṇavidhiṃ param /
children.translated_text: Having thus praised with that divine supreme entreaty,
generating compassion for the disciple, the glorious <s>guru</s>, ocean of virtues,
becoming serene-faced, compassionate, and delighted,
should cause the disciple to hear the divine <s>samaya</s> (commitment), the supreme arising from the <s>yogatantra</s>.
Then the concentrated <s>ācārya</s> (master) should generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening),

children.text: kalaśe vātha śaṃkhe vā bodhicittaṃ nidhāya ca //
children.translated_text: and having placed the <s>bodhicitta</s> in a vase or a conch shell,
he should then summon that disciple, blessed by all <s>Buddhas</s>,
and bestow the <s>samaya</s> upon him, endowed with the seal of the Conqueror.
The <s>abhiṣeka</s> (initiation) should be given by the second <s>vajra</s>-holder,
with auspicious, delightful sounds and various musical instruments.
With the initiation of the three realms, the disciple, with bowed head and palms joined,
being permitted, should then give that which he is prompted to offer.
The garland, water, awakened <s>vajra</s>, <s>ghaṇṭā</s> (bell), and mirror,
the name, the <s>ācārya</s>, and the permission—this is the sequence of <s>abhiṣeka</s> (initiation).

body.text:
tataḥ samarpayet tasya bāhyābhisaṃbodhilakṣaṇam /
saṃpradāye yadāvāptaṃ guruparvakramāgatam // iti /

children.text: toye nirmalake nadīsarasi vā binduśca yo līnakaḥ /
children.translated_text: In pure water, in a river or a lake, and a <s>bindu</s> (drop) that has dissolved,
that which is pure, taught gradually as undifferentiated—the <s>yogī</s> should always contemplate.
In a mirror, the cessation of wind proceeds gradually; that is not perceived,
the grasping of the aggregate (<s>piṇḍagrāha</s>)—thus the gradual process is contemplated by the systematic practitioner.

body.translated_text:
Then one should bestow upon him the external mark of awakening,
that which was obtained in the lineage, coming through the succession of <s>gurus</s>. Thus:

children.translated_text: Beyond the meditation on all limbs, free from the imagined and the imaginable,
beyond <s>mātrā</s> (measure) and <s>bindu</s> (drop)—this is the supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>.
That which enters into all existences, pure in form and formlessness,
the awakened, aroused mind—the <s>maṇḍala</s> in the form of a <s>maṇḍala</s>.

body.text:
astīti nāstīti ubhe 'pi antā śuddhī aśuddhīti ime 'pi antā /
tasmādubhe antavivarjayitvā madhye 'pi sthānaṃ na karoti paṇḍitaḥ // iti /

children.translated_text: The meaning is 'space is infinite'—the great abode of all beings.
<s>Vibhūti</s> (power) is the king, the glorious lord, the fulfiller of all hopes.

body.translated_text:
'Exists' and 'does not exist'—both are extremes; 'pure' and 'impure'—these too are extremes.
Therefore, having abandoned both extremes, the wise one does not take a stand even in the middle. Thus:

children.text: aho buddha aho buddha aho dharmasya deśanā /
children.translated_text: Oh <s>Buddha</s>! Oh <s>Buddha</s>! Oh, the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>!
Pure in the essence of truth, pure in meaning — homage to you, <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening)!

body.translated_text: End of the seventh chapter, the resolution of doubts concerning the blending of <s>paramārthasatya</s> (ultimate truth). // 7 //
8. Eighth Chapter

body.text:
sthūlaṃ śabdamayaṃ prāhuḥ sūkṣmaṃ cittāmayantathā /
cittayā rahitaṃ yat tad yogināṃ paramaṃ padam // iti /

children.text: svasaṃvedyaṃ tu tattattvaṃ vaktuṃ nānyasya pāryate /
children.translated_text: That reality (<s>tattva</s>) is to be known by oneself; it cannot be spoken to another.

children.text: bhaktibhāvanayā gamyaṃ na gamyaṃ cānyathā nu tat //
children.translated_text: It is reached through devotion and meditation; it is not reached otherwise.

body.translated_text:
The gross is said to be of the nature of sound; the subtle is likewise of the nature of mind;
that which is free from mind — that is the supreme state of the <s>yogins</s>.

children.translated_text: Having known the reality, then cultivating devotion day and night,
in that supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the peaceful, unsurpassed state,
then, through the power of that devotion, produced by the force of meditation,
there arises in it a form, born of supreme bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), beyond description.
Arising in the form of a flash, sparkling with the form of dissolution,
illuminating all this — <s>bhūr</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svar</s> — the moving and the unmoving.
Through the power of meditation, auspicious, having the nature of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (means),
freed from all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), adorned with all marks,
born from the knowledge of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), free from duality, supremely auspicious,
endowed with the best of all forms, free from grasped and grasper,
knowledge illusion-like, pure, translucent, naturally stainless,
beyond sound, smell, and taste, and likewise free from touch,
it is seen by the supreme one alone, in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), with the eye of knowledge —
divine, like a shadow or illusion, endowed with a divine form.
With garlands of flashing waves of knowledge, of manifold and various embodiments,
those who meditate on reality obtain a body resembling a rainbow (<s>Indra</s>'s bow).
Through the power of the practice of meditation and the observance of <s>samayas</s> (commitments),

children.text: īdṛśaṃ prāpyate rūpaṃ na vācyaṃ yajjinairapi //
children.translated_text: such a form is obtained, which cannot be described even by the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors).

children.text: yatra kāyo na vākcittaṃ sthānaṃ yatsarvagaṃ param /
children.translated_text: Where there is no body, speech, or mind — that state which is all-pervading and supreme —
there, through the power of the transmission (<s>saṃpradāya</s>), one's own form is made manifest.

body.text:
aho suvismayakaramaho śāntamatīndriyam /
aho paramagambhīraṃ buddhatvaṃ padamuttamam // iti /
aho vajra aho vajra aho vajrasya deśanā /
yatra na kāyavākcittaṃ tatra rūpaṃ vibhāvyate // iti /
body.translated_text:
Oh, how wondrous! Oh, how peaceful, beyond the senses!
Oh, how profoundly deep is <s>Buddhahood</s>, the supreme state!
Oh <s>Vajra</s>! Oh <s>Vajra</s>! Oh, the teaching of the <s>Vajra</s>!
Where there is no body, speech, or mind, there a form is made manifest.

children.translated_text: The revered master (<s>Bhaṭṭārakapāda</s>) also said:

children.text: śauśīryaṃ nāsti te kāye māṃsāsthirudhiraṃ na ca /
children.translated_text: There is no hollowness in your body, neither flesh, bones, nor blood;
like a rainbow in the sky, you have displayed your body.

body.text:
nāmayo nāśuciḥ kāye kṣuttṛṣṇāsaṃbhavau na ca /
tvayā lokānuvṛttyarthaṃ darśitā laukikī kriyā // iti /
body.translated_text:
There is no disease or impurity in the body, nor the arising of hunger and thirst;
you have displayed worldly activity for the sake of conforming to the world.
In the <s>Sarvakalpasamuccaya</s> also it is said:

body.text:
gṛhītvā hṛdayaṃ śuddhaṃ vajradehavibhāvanā /
dṛḍhaṃ sāramasauśīryaṃ vajrakāyaṃ sa labdhavān // iti /
khasamā virajā vararūpadharā aśarīra alakṣaṇa prajñasutā /
sugambhīraguṇodadhi kāruṇikā dada mūrdhni pāṇi mama apratimā // iti /
body.translated_text:
Having taken the pure heart-essence, through the meditation on the <s>vajra</s> body,
firm, essential, without hollowness — he has obtained the <s>vajrakāya</s> (diamond body).
Equal to space, dustless, bearing the finest form, bodiless, without marks, sons of wisdom,
profoundly deep ocean of qualities, compassionate ones — place your incomparable hand upon my crown.
End of the eighth chapter, the resolution of doubts concerning the blending of <s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇadhātu</s> (the realm of non-abiding nirvāṇa). // 8 //
9. Ninth Chapter

body.text:
phalena hetumāmudrya phalamāmudrya hetunā /
vibhāvyamanyathāsiddhiṃ kalpakoṭirna jāyate // iti /
vajrasattvo mahārājaścodanīyo muhurmuhuḥ // iti /

children.translated_text: Abandoning the posture of extending the feet, giving up the box of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
one should accomplish the foremost <s>Vajrasattva</s>, with a mind always diligent.

body.translated_text:
Sealing the cause with the fruit, and sealing the fruit with the cause,
if one contemplates <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) otherwise, it will not arise even in <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>.
<s>Vajrasattva</s>, the great king, must be urged again and again.

body.text:
kaukṛtyastyānamiddhādīn parityajya prayatnataḥ /
anyathā naiva siddhiḥ syāt kalpakoṭiśatairapi // iti /
bhikṣubhāve sthitā ye 'tra ye tu tarkaratā narāḥ /
vṛddhabhāve sthitā ye tu teṣāṃ tattvaṃ na deśayet // iti /

children.text: upāyarahitaṃ jñānaṃ śikṣā cāpi hi deśitā /
children.translated_text: Knowledge without skillful means, and training also, has been taught
for <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), O Great Hero; understand them thus.

body.translated_text:
Abandoning remorse, torpor, drowsiness, and the like with effort;
otherwise, <s>siddhi</s> will never be attained even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>.
For those who abide in the state of a monk, and those who delight in philosophical speculation,
and those who abide in the state of old age — to them the reality should not be taught.

body.text:
mūlasūtre 'pyāha-
daśakuśalān karmapathānicchanti jñānavarjitāḥ // iti /
śrāvakayānamaśikṣatha bhikṣo bodhicariyata tatra carīye /
bodhicarīṃ cara buddhaguṇeṣu eṣa nidānabhaviṣya svayaṃbhūḥ // iti /
duṣkarairniyamaistīrvrairmūrtiḥ śuṣyati duḥkhitā /
duḥkhād vikṣipyate cittaṃ vikṣepāt siddhiranyathā // iti /
body.translated_text:
In the <s>Mūlasūtra</s> also it is said:
Those devoid of knowledge desire the ten paths of wholesome action.
Learn the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, O monk; practice the <s>bodhicaryā</s> (bodhisattva conduct) therein.
Practice the <s>bodhicaryā</s> in the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>; this is the cause of becoming a <s>Svayaṃbhū</s> (Self-Arisen One).
Through difficult and severe austerities, the body withers in pain;
from pain the mind is distracted; from distraction, <s>siddhi</s> goes astray.

body.text:
mūlasūtre 'pyāha-
duṣkarairniyamaistīvraiḥ sevyamāno na siddhyati /
sarvakāmopabhogaistu sevayaṃścāśu siddhyati // iti /

children.text: rāgo dveṣaśca mohaśca traya ete viṣaṅgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Desire (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) — these three are associated with poison;
they become poison indeed when practiced wrongly.

body.text: amṛtatvaṃ punaryānti, amṛtena tu sevitāḥ // iti /

children.text: badhyati yena jaḍaḥ parimucyati tena budhaḥ /
children.translated_text: That by which the fool is bound, by that very thing the wise one is liberated.
Through the meditation on awakening, all this is reversed.

body.translated_text: But they become nectar when practiced with the nectar method.

body.text:
yena mūḍhāḥ prabadhyante śīryante rauravāntike /
taireva hi vimucyante sukhaṃ prajñābalena tu // iti /

children.translated_text: Now I shall proclaim the supreme, all-encompassing,
the <s>Sarvabuddhasamāyogaḍākinījālasaṃvara</s> (the Union of All Buddhas, the Net of <s>Ḍākinīs</s> Vow).

body.translated_text:
That by which the deluded are bound and perish near the <s>Raurava</s> hell,
by those very things they are liberated and find happiness, through the power of wisdom.

children.text: rahasye parame ramye sarvātmani sadā sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the supreme, delightful secret, always abiding in the self of all,
the glorious one, the arising of <s>Vajrasattva</s>, consisting of all <s>Buddhas</s>, is bliss.
Adorned with the great divine jewel-net of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and so forth,
with brilliant canopies hung with suspended bells,
with <s>vajra</s> songs and worship performed through song and music,
with the application of flowers, incense, lamps, fragrances, and the like,
they adorn the dwelling or in gardens and so forth,
the <s>Sarvabuddhasamāyogaḍākinījālasaṃvara</s>.
There, first establishing a seat producing the bliss of soft touch,
covered with a cloth of universal lotuses — that is the entirely pure seat.
The union of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the transformation of the Lord of <s>Yoga</s>,
where they transform into the form of the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>,
consisting of all elements (<s>dhātus</s>), or consisting of the vital root,
the performance of the <s>siddhi-mudrā</s> (accomplishment-seal) with the faces of one's own presiding deity,
whether cast, assembled, consecrated, or beautifully painted,
one should prepare the emblem-seal (<s>cihnamudrā</s>) with various reflections.
On those seats, one should place all the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital energies) in their proper positions,
square, with four doors, adorned with four arched gateways,
with <s>vajra</s>, jewel, lotus, and other door-guardians joined,
with a well-adorned consort facing one's own presiding deity,
one should prepare the circle-<s>maṇḍala</s> (assembly), beautiful with one's own seals and emblems.
Square, with four doors, adorned with four arched gateways,
connected with four cords, embellished with eight pillars,
fashioned with necklaces and half-necklaces, adorned with silk garlands and festoons,
resplendent with bells and banners, decorated with whisks and the like,
with half-moon and <s>vajra</s>-pointed corners, at the junctures of the doorway projections,
adorned with variegated cloths of bird, woman, and serpent-head designs.
With the enjoyments of all goddesses, served according to pleasure,
through the <s>yoga</s> of one's own presiding deity, one should worship one's own self.
Worshipped through the practice, with the bliss of all <s>yogas</s>,
savoring it, one attains <s>siddhi</s> through supreme <s>yoga</s>.
Through this essence of all <s>Buddhas</s>, through the bliss of the elixir,
one may accomplish the longevity of the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s> — youth, health, and true happiness.
The great body of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the eloquence of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the great mind of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the great celebration of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the great king of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the supreme lord of all <s>Vajradharas</s>,
the lord of all <s>Lokeśvaras</s>, the supreme sovereign of all jewels.

body.text:
tābhiḥ saṃramyamāṇastu yātyutpattiṃ tu gacchataḥ /
sarvadevīmahāsidhya(ddha)ścakravartī prasidhyati // iti /
pratyahaṃ pratimāsaṃ vā pratisaṃvatsaraṃ tathā /
yathādhiṣṭhānato vāpi nāṭayed buddhasaṃvaram // iti /

children.text: utthito vā niṣaṇṇo vā caṃkraman vā yathāsthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether standing, sitting, walking, or however positioned,

children.text: praharṣan vā jalpan vā yatra tatra yathā tathā //
children.translated_text: whether rejoicing or conversing, wherever and however,

body.translated_text:
Delighting with those consorts, one goes to the arising that comes;
by the great <s>siddhi</s> of all goddesses, one attains the <s>cakravartin</s> (universal sovereignty).
Daily, monthly, or yearly,
or according to one's resolution, one should perform the <s>Buddha-saṃvara</s> (Buddha vow).

children.translated_text: whatever comes through the path of the senses, by its very nature,
through the <s>yoga</s> of non-concentration, one should carry all as consisting of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
Equal to space, of the form of space, like an infinite ocean,
the <s>dharma</s> of desire (<s>rāga</s>) is the method; hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) is the display; play is the elaboration.
Only a mere outline of the subject has been grasped, for the purpose of instructing disciples;
who can bear to speak of the teaching of desire through many lifetimes?

body.translated_text: End of the ninth chapter, by the method of the glorious <s>Sarvabuddhasamāyogaḍākinījālasaṃvara</s>: the resolution of doubts concerning the blending of the expansion of the awakening of the <s>Dharma</s>-arising of <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct. // 9 //
10. Tenth Chapter

children.translated_text: In the regions of a great forest, adorned with fruits and flowers,
on a solitary mountain, one should accomplish this collection of <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations).

body.text: sevayan kāmaguṇān pañca jñānārthirāgiṇaḥ sadā // iti /

children.translated_text: The cultivation of body, speech, and mind through the <s>vajras</s> (adamantine essences) of body, speech, and mind —
that work should be done in its own nature; [thereby] the minor <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) is obtained.

body.translated_text: always enjoying the five qualities of desire, the one who seeks knowledge is passionate.

children.translated_text: An image bearing matted hair and a crown, great, resembling white color,
should be made according to the prescribed rites, enveloped by <s>mantra</s> and <s>saṃvara</s> (vow).
Taking a sixteen-year-old girl adorned with all ornaments,
beautiful-faced, wide-eyed — having obtained her, one should perform the observance of <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge).
One should meditate with the emblems of <s>Locanā</s>, <s>Pāṇḍarā</s>, <s>Saṃbhogā</s>, and <s>Vajra</s>,
one who knows the method of <s>mudrā</s> (seal) and <s>mantra</s>, well-trained in <s>mantra</s> and <s>tantra</s>.
One should make her a wife belonging to the <s>Tathāgata</s> family, established in <s>Buddha</s>-awakening.
The one of great vows should perform the secret worship (<s>guhyapūjā</s>) at the four junctures.
One should prepare all food and eatables with tubers, roots, and fruits.
Thus one quickly becomes a <s>Buddha</s>, a lord, an ocean of great knowledge.
In six months alone one attains all that — there is no doubt about this.
The <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) of firm determination should always wander in the forest seeking alms.
They, struck with fear, give food that is divinely adorned.

children.text: atikramanti yadi vajrātmā nāśaṃ vajrākṣaraṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text: If one of <s>vajra</s>-nature transgresses, the <s>vajrākṣara</s> (adamantine syllable) would be destroyed.

body.text:
surīṃ nāgīṃ mahāyakṣīmasurīṃ mānuṣīmapi /
prāpya vidyāvrataṃ kāryaṃ trivajrajñānasevitam // iti /

children.translated_text: Through the union of the two faculties, in the interval of the practice,
the joyful mind in the sage's accomplishment is called <s>mahāsukha</s> (great bliss).

body.translated_text: Having obtained a <s>surī</s> (goddess), <s>nāgī</s> (serpent woman), great <s>yakṣī</s>, <s>asurī</s>, or even a human woman, one should perform the observance of <s>vidyā</s>, cultivated through the knowledge of the three <s>vajras</s>.
End of the tenth chapter, the investigation of doubts regarding the conduct-synthesis free from conceptual elaboration.
11. Eleventh Chapter

children.translated_text: On secluded mountains, at rivers and springs,
and even in cremation grounds and such places, this collection of meditations should be practiced.
The one who knows reality should always abandon the preliminary practices and such in accordance with reality.
Having given up the ego-identity of <s>Vajrasattva</s>, one should not create it elsewhere.

children.text: prayogā api na budhyante śuddhatattve vyavasthite /
children.translated_text: The preliminary practices too are not realized when one is established in pure reality (<s>śuddhatattva</s>).
By the yoga of the state of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), that is investigated to the extent possible.
For one who abides in the state of essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>) and is endowed with divine skillful means,
whatever is prompted by ritual procedure is accomplished without deliberation.
Through the power of meditation-yoga, it manifests of its own accord —
all that, in a single moment, whatever has the mark of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment).
Seeing internal <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the rest is called <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight);
visualizing <s>Akṣobhya</s> and the others in due order constitutes <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding).

body.text:
anayorniḥsvabhāvatvāt tathatāśāntasaṃjñakam /
tathatāmaṇḍale yogī sarvabuddhān praveśayed // iti /

children.translated_text: In the great terror of the fire of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, even ashes are not released.

children.text: na tatra vidyate tattvaṃ nendriyārthā na dhātavaḥ //
children.translated_text: There, reality does not exist, nor do sense-objects, nor elements.

body.translated_text: Due to the essencelessness of both of these, it is called 'peaceful suchness' (<s>tathatā</s>). In the <s>maṇḍala</s> of suchness, the <s>yogī</s> should cause all <s>Buddhas</s> to enter.

children.text: nirvikalpo yadā viraḥ sthitiṃ hitvā tu laukikīm /
children.translated_text: When the hero is free from conceptual construction (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), having abandoned worldly abiding,

children.text: ācaret sarvakāryāṇi buddhāḥ paśyanti tat tadā //
children.translated_text: and performs all activities — the <s>Buddhas</s> behold that then.
One should conduct oneself with skill like a child, with all doubts completely severed.

children.text: nirābhogo yadā yogī tadā varṣanti saṃpadaḥ //
children.translated_text: When the <s>yogī</s> is without effort (<s>nirābhoga</s>), then accomplishments rain down.
For those endowed with every sin, well-established in the veil of delusion,
through the yoga of the vow of madness (<s>unmattavrata</s>), in six months come infallible accomplishments.
One sees all <s>Buddhas</s> oneself and is filled with all desires;

children.text: na kṣīṇo na ca hānitvaṃ svecchāyurjāyate vapuḥ //
children.translated_text: neither diminished nor declining, a body of one's own desired lifespan arises.
The unsurpassed, supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is attained effortlessly;
without exertion, all who are eager for the bliss of desires achieve accomplishment.
One should always go to the profound state, whether standing, sitting, or reclining.
Through skill in luminous knowledge (<s>prabhāsvarajñāna</s>), this is ever the mark of <s>yogīs</s>.
Through this yoga of meditation, the mind-jewel becomes firm,
and the <s>Buddhas</s> established in awakening bestow their blessings (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>).
Having thus become [established], one who is absorbed should meditate, devoted to cultivation,
as long as the mind is not wearied — the wise one with concentrated mind.
When wearied, one should afterward wander about, acting as one pleases;
one should cultivate vast <s>bodhi</s> with eyes slightly opened.

body.translated_text: Laughing, chatting, sometimes standing, sometimes setting things in motion —
with mind attached to meditation, so that weariness does not arise.

body.text:
evaṃ samādhiyuktasya nirvikalpasya mantriṇaḥ /
kālāvadhiṃ parityajya siddhyate 'nuttaraṃ padam // iti /
sūkṣmarūpaṃ laghusparśaṃ vyāptisaṃprāptimeva ca /
prakāśaṃ caiva sthairyaṃ ca vaśitvaṃ kāmāvasānikam // iti /

children.translated_text: Having attained the supreme knowledge of awakening, one sees the <s>Buddha</s> of great radiance,
and one sees oneself as the <s>sambhogakāya</s> (enjoyment body) of the <s>Buddha</s> quickly.

body.translated_text: Thus, for the <s>mantrin</s> (mantra-adept) united with <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and free from conceptual construction, abandoning the limit of time, the unsurpassed state is accomplished. Subtle form, light touch, the attainment of pervasion, radiance, stability, mastery, and the culmination of desire [are the eight qualities].

children.translated_text: One sees oneself worshipped by the great beings of the three realms,
and constantly by <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> with the five qualities of desire.
One always sees oneself worshipped, arisen from great knowledge,
as <s>Vajrasattva</s>, the great image, <s>Vajradharma</s>, of great renown.
In dreams one sees one's own image, the great and glorious secret <s>vajra</s>;
the great <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are <s>vajra</s>-holders bow down.
One will see such dreams, bestowing the <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments) of body, speech, and mind —
a divine maiden adorned with all ornaments, delightful to the mind.
Seeing a boy or a girl, one attains <s>siddhi</s>;
one certainly sees oneself established in the <s>Buddha</s>-fields of all <s>Buddhas</s> of the ten directions.
With joyful mind and self, they give the delightful <s>dharma</s>-treasury;
the body engaged in the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, surrounded by all beings —

body.text:
paśyate yogasamaye dhyānavajrapratiṣṭhitaḥ // iti /
nāpaneyamataḥ kiñcit prakṣeptavyaṃ na kiñcan /
draṣṭavyaṃ bhūtato bhūtaṃ bhūtadarśī vimucyate // iti /
uktaṃ ca suvarṇaprabhāsasūtre-
body.translated_text: one sees this at the time of yoga, established in the <s>vajra</s> of meditation. Nothing is to be removed from this, nothing is to be added; what is real should be seen as real — the one who sees reality is liberated. As it is also said in the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa Sūtra</s>:

children.text: na buddhaḥ parinirvāti na dharmaḥ parihīyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> does not pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; the <s>Dharma</s> does not decline.
For the purpose of ripening beings, he displays <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.
It is also said in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra</s>:
Nothing whatsoever arises here through conditions, nor is it destroyed;
conditions that arise and cease are merely imagined.
Therefore it is said:

children.text: yena yena hi bhāvena manaḥ saṃyujyate nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: By whatever object the minds of people are united,
they become identified with that, like a wish-fulfilling jewel of universal form.
Birth is the conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>); death is indeed the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>).

children.text: kramadvayasyāsya gurukṛpāto jñātā bhaved yaḥ sa bhaviṣyabuddhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Whoever knows these two stages through the guru's compassion — he will be a future <s>Buddha</s>.
Entry into the non-duality of the two truths is of the nature of non-annihilation and without distinction;
that there is only oneness of these two — whoever knows this is the liberated one.

children.text: girīndramūrdhnaḥ prapatet tu kaścid neccheccyutiṃ sa cyavate tathāpi /
children.translated_text: Someone might fall from the peak of the king of mountains, and not wish to fall — yet he falls even so.
Through the grace of the guru and the instruction bestowed, one might not wish for liberation — yet even so, one is liberated.
Having observed the incapacity of beings for the realization of reality, looking upon the world
as if from the scattered spray of waves in a vast ocean, like a spark from a lamp,

children.text: kiñcit kiñcidupetya saṃcitavatā grantho mayāyaṃ kṛto
children.translated_text: having gathered little by little and accumulated, this text has been composed by me.
For those fortunate ones who are not afraid of conventional truth — from this may there be purity.

body.translated_text: End of the eleventh chapter, the investigation of doubts regarding the conduct-synthesis of absolute freedom from conceptual elaboration.
This <s>Caryāmelāvaṇapradīpa</s> (Lamp for the Integration of Practices) is completed.
This is the composition of the great master <s>Āryadeva</s>.
